title: What does VaultSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of VaultSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, VaultSet modifies the configurable properties of a single-asset vault controlled by the caller. [1]

Only properties the feature permits to change can be updated; ownership of configuration authority does not imply unrestricted access to participant assets. Review the exact fields and dependent lending arrangements before signing. The validated update proves a parameter change, not that the new settings are commercially suitable or approved by a regulator. [1]

The VaultSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using VaultSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
